index.title: Faint Lines Without Dimming
index.prompt: A 6 by 6 image holds a bright vertical line that a PGD attack has dimmed while adding faint horizontal lines across rows 2 and 5. Try the faint lines on their own: add a to every pixel of rows 2 and 5, keep the line at 1, and find the vertical filter's pooled total at a = 0.4 plus the smallest a at which the network stops preferring vertical. 2 parts.
index.answer: Worked solutions are given part by part on the problem page. Attempt each part on paper before revealing it.

theory.title: Faint Lines Without Dimming
overview: PGD's attacked image at $\varepsilon = 0.4$ makes two changes: it dims the line to 0.6 in rows 1, 3, 4 and 6, and it adds faint lines of 0.4 across rows 2 and 5. Try the second change on its own. Add $a$ to every pixel of rows 2 and 5 and leave the line at 1 everywhere. Its pixels in rows 2 and 5 stay at 1, because the clip holds them there, so no pixel moves by more than $a$:

setup.tex:
\begin{array}{ccccccc}
\text{Row} & \text{Col 1} & \text{Col 2} & \text{Col 3} & \text{Col 4} & \text{Col 5} & \text{Col 6} \\ \hline
1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
2 & a & a & 1 & a & a & a \\
3 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
4 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
5 & a & a & 1 & a & a & a \\
6 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0
\end{array}

setup.p: The network is the running example's: the two filters, ReLU, 2 × 2 max pooling and scores of a quarter of each pooled map's total.

prompt.p: At $a = 0.4$, what is the total of the vertical pooled map?

answer.p: Every window of three rows holds exactly one of rows 2 and 5, so every row of a map has the same pattern.

**Vertical map.** Over columns 2 to 4, a plain row reads 0, 1, 0 and gives 2, and a faint row reads $a$, 1, $a$ and gives $2 - 2a$, so each value is $6 - 2a$. Over columns 1 to 3 a plain row gives $-1$ and a faint row $-a + 2a - 1 = a - 1$, a total of $a - 3$, below 0. Over columns 3 to 5 it is the same, and over columns 4 to 6 every row gives 0. After ReLU only $6 - 2a$ is left, the pooled map is $6 - 2a$, 0 in each row, and the vertical total is $12 - 4a$.

**Horizontal map.** The filter takes $-1$, 2, $-1$ times the sums of the window's top, middle and bottom rows. A plain row sums to 1 when the window covers column 3 (map columns 1 to 3) and to 0 over columns 4 to 6. A faint row sums to $1 + 2a$ and $3a$ in the same windows. Map rows 1 and 4 have the faint row in the middle, so they get twice the faint sum minus twice the plain sum: $4a$ in map columns 1 to 3 and $6a$ in map column 4. Map rows 2 and 3 have it at an edge and come out negative, so ReLU keeps

answer.tex: 4a, \ 4a, \ 4a, \ 6a \quad \text{in map rows 1 and 4, and 0 in rows 2 and 3.}

answer.p: Each pooled row is $4a, 6a$, and the horizontal total is $20a$.

At $a = 0.4$ the pooled vertical map is $6 - 2a, 0$ in each row, which is 5.2 and 0, and the total the classification layer scores is $12 - 4a = 10.4$. The horizontal total is $20a = 8$, so the scores are 2.6 and 2 and
against 0.953 for the untouched line. The faint rows cost the vertical total 1.6 of its 12 and give the horizontal map 8 out of nothing, but the network still says vertical.

prompt.p: What is the smallest $a$ at which the network no longer prefers "vertical", that is, $p(\text{vertical}) \le 0.5$?

answer.p: The scores are $0.25(12 - 4a) = 3 - a$ and $0.25 \times 20a = 5a$. They tie when $3 - a = 5a$, at $a = 0.5$.

PGD's image does both things. The line dimmed to $1 - a$ makes the vertical total $12(1 - a)$. The faint rows now stand out by $3a$ in every window, $(1 + 2a) - (1 - a)$ where the window covers column 3 and $3a - 0$ where it does not, which makes all four pooled horizontal values $6a$ and the total $24a$. The scores are $3 - 3a$ and $6a$, equal at $a = 1/3$, which fits the page's PGD column, 0.574 at 0.3 and 0.354 at 0.4. Dimming the line costs no more budget than brightening the background, and it helps twice: it lowers the vertical score and raises the horizontal one. With the faint lines alone, a budget of 0.4 is not enough.
